results.title: Public Cloud new pricing details, starting October 1, 2026
results.author: Octave Klaba
highlights:
Our Public Cloud instance prices are changing on October 1, 2026. For an identical configuration, the increase in price ranges from 1.4% to 21.9%, dependent on size.

This does not affect the calculated price, which will remain unchanged. However, two of the resources that were previously included in our instances — local storage and public IPv4 address — will now be billed separately.

...

## The three-line model

Find the essential points of the new model summarized here below.

The hourly price of instances does not change. This price will be identical before and after October 1, 2026, for all ranges.

Local storage and public IPv4 addresses, which were previously included in the price of Generation 3 instances (B3, C3, R3), are now two separate billing lines. Local storage is now becoming a full-fledged storage class called Local Low Latency.

...

The new rate takes effect on 

September 1, 2026.

...

## Change schedule

| Date | Step |
| --- | --- |
| End of August 2026 | Update of the prices on the website |
| September 1, 2026 | Launch of the new Savings Plans grid, informing of the clients concerned |
| October 1, 2026 | Local storage and IPv4 address billed separately |

highlights:
As for Bare Metal and Cloud servers, they are designed and assembled in our two plants. The high-volume orders you place with us every year has allowed us to build long-standing supplier relationships, significantly reducing our supply chain issues. We apply a price update in the second month of each quarter, effective for the remainder of the quarter. The increase takes effect immediately and in full, no different from any hardware or cloud provider.

...

We’ve ruled out a flat increase across the entire catalogue. Our teams reviewed every range, model by model, to adjust only what is genuinely affected, in line with the actual cost impact. Any range or generation not listed in this article retains its current price.

To stop new solutions becoming unaffordable, we’ve also applied an increase to services already in production.

...

- 1 July 2026: new rates for memory and storage options apply to orders from this date onwards
- 11 August 2026: new server configuration pricing apply to new orders from this date onwards
- 1 October 2026: new rates apply to servers already running, taking effect on the subscription renewal date

Scope: Advance (Gen 2024 and 2026), Game (Gen 2026), Scale and High Grade (Gen 2024 and 2026). The Kimsufi, So you Start and Rise ranges are not affected, nor are generations before Gen 2024.

Service performance, availability and support levels, as well as your SLAs and contractual terms stay the same. This adjustment concerns the price only. You keep the included DDoS protection and network performance, all still within a sovereign, European cloud.

results.title: OVHcloud increases prices by up to 87 percent due to more expensive RAM
results.author: Michaël Aussems
highlights:
The AI boom is driving up the prices of memory and storage. OVHcloud is therefore adjusting its rates starting from the third quarter of 2026.

OVHcloud is increasing its prices because the costs of RAM and storage are rising sharply under the pressure of AI. Founder Octave Klaba announced this on X. “As you know, AI has a very large impact on the prices of the RAM and storage we use to build our data center servers,” he writes. Purchase prices remain uncertain: OVHcloud must order monthly without a guaranteed price and without knowing the actual demand.

## Large increase for bare metal

For dedicated servers, the entry-level ranges Kimsufi, So You Start, and Rise remain unchanged. The more expensive ranges will increase: an average of 28 percent for the 2024 generation and 51 percent for the 2026 generation. The outlier is the Game range, which will become 87 percent more expensive on the latest generation.

Existing customers are being spared with a reduced rate on already installed options. “A customer who is already equipped will therefore receive an increase that is three to six times lower than for a new order,” says Klaba. Nothing changes during an ongoing contract.

...

For its public cloud offering, OVHcloud is not increasing the compute hourly rate. Instead, the company is splitting the bill. “Instead of increasing the prices of the ‘all-inclusive’ instances, we are changing the business model to be comparable to our competitors,” says Klaba.

Two items that were previously included in the Gen3 instances (B3, C3, and R3) will be listed as separate lines on the invoice starting October 1: the Block Storage “Low Latency” and the IPv4 address. The hourly rate for computing power therefore remains the same on paper, but the total cost per instance increases. This net effect ranges from 1.4 to 21.9 percent, depending on the size: small instances feel it the most, large ones hardly at all, because the IP address and storage cost the same fixed amount for everyone.

results.title: OvhCloud augmente ses prix pour la deuxième fois en 2026 - ZDNET
results.author: Louis Adam
highlights:
OvhCloud a publié hier le détail de ses nouveaux tarifs au second semestre 2026. Comme l'avait annoncé Octave Klaba, la hausse des prix des composants et de la RAM se répercute sur les fournisseurs de services cloud. 

 Par Louis Adam 

Publié le 18/08/2026 à 12:30 | Mis à jour le 02/09/2026 à 14:31 

 

Ce n'est pas une surprise, mais ça n'est jamais agréable : OvhCloud a publié hier le détail des évolutions de sa grille tarifaire pour le second semestre 2026, et la facture se révèle salée. Les hausses affectent les offres Baremetal et Public Cloud, mais la société précise que ses offres d'entrée de gamme, Kimsufi, So You Start et Rise ne sont pas affectées.

## Des augmentations à partir de septembre

En moyenne, les prix augmentent de 28% pour les offres s'appuyant sur des équipements de la Gen 2024, et de 51% sur la Gen 2026. Les nouveaux prix s'appliqueront aux configurations de serveur à partir du 1er septembre. Mais les augmentations affecteront également le matériel déjà en production à compter du 1er octobre, sur les gammes Advance, Game, Scale et High Grade.

Octave Klaba avait annoncé l'augmentation des prix à venir dans un message sur X en début de semaine dernière. Le fondateur de la société expliquait alors que la hausse de ces tarifs était poussée par l'augmentation des prix de la RAM et des équipements que la société utilise pour fournir ses clients. Il déplore une situation très frustrante, mais rappelle qu'OVHCloud fait son possible pour limiter la hausse des prix et rester transparent à l'égard de ses clients.

...

L'enjeu pour OVHCloud est de taille : "le contexte mondial nous impose une discipline très stricte pour, tout simplement, continuer à livrer les nouvelles commandes" résume Octave Klaba. Et la situation ne devrait pas s'améliorer tout de suite : le dirigeant estime que l'augmentation devrait continuer en 2027, voire plus tard. "Nous pensons que cette situation va durer jusqu'en 2028, avec un retour à la normale espéré en 2029" veut croire Octave Klaba. Pour limiter l'impact de futures augmentations, le dirigeant invite ses clients à souscrire à des offres longues durées, payées à l'avance, avant le 1er octobre.

...

Cette augmentation est principalement liée à l'essor des technologies d'intelligence artificielle, très consommatrice en matière de mémoire RAM et de puissance de calcul, et dont les principaux

...

Du côté d'AWS, la société a annoncé une hausse mesurée du prix de ses GPU en début d'année 2026, et Microsoft revoyait à la hausse les tarifs de ses offres Office 365 au début du mois de juillet, mais pas de hausse généralisée pour l'instant. Les analystes s'attendent néanmoins à ce que les tensions sur les prix des composants finissent par se répercuter sur l'ensemble des acteurs.

results.title: OVHcloud to raise dedicated server prices by up to 87 percent from September - DCD
results.author: Georgia Butler
highlights:
OVHcloud's CEO, Octave Klaba, has warned that the company will have to raise prices for its dedicated server offerings due to the rising costs of memory.

As reported by The Register, Klaba noted in a post on X that the company has now had the latest details on RAM and disk prices for the upcoming quarter, which "allows us to finalize the price impacts for new public cloud and baremetal orders."

...

Pricing increases vary from product to product, but Klaba said the average will see a 28 percent increase for "Gen 2024" hardware, and 51 percent for "Gen 2026."

The biggest increase is for Gen 2026 gaming infrastructure, up 87 percent.

On-going commitments won't see price increases, and customers can lock in current prices by subscribing with upfront payments.

...

Since the post on X, a blog post has been shared by OVHcloud that explains the price increases further and why hardware from 2024 is also included. "To prevent new offers from becoming unaffordable, we have also chosen to apply a price increase to services already in use by our existing customers, but only for very recent equipment using the latest generation of RAM: DDR5. This makes the increase more moderate for everyone, and allows us to continue offering you new equipment at an affordable price."

...

Klaba added: "We are subject to a price update in the second month of each quarter, applicable to the entire quarter: we experience the increase immediately and in full, like any other player in the hardware or cloud market."

results.title: OVHcloud raises prices due to AI demand | iMasters
results.author: Redação iMasters
highlights:
OVHcloud will raise prices across much of its catalog this fall (Northern Hemisphere), and the cause isn't in the products that will get more expensive. According to an InfoQ report, founder Octave Klaba attributes the move to the accelerated buildout of AI infrastructure, which is pulling manufacturing capacity away from the components any ordinary server is built with.

...

The numbers come from OVHcloud's own purchasing. Indexing June 2025 as base 100, memory reached 604 by June 2026, SSDs hit 323, and HDDs hit 148. In other words: the company now pays roughly 6x the RAM price it paid a year ago. And the forecast gets worse:

> This month, June 2026, we're paying 6x the RAM price we paid in June 2025. We already know it will be 9x in September 2026, while forecasts for early 2027 stand at 12x!?

...

The increase isn't uniform. Customers renting the 2026-edition gaming servers face the steepest hike, 87%, while other recent servers rise between 40% and 59%, all effective from September. Customers on 2024-generation hardware see smaller increases upon renewal, which Klaba estimates to be three to six times lower than on a new order. Older lines, including Kimsufi, Rise, and earlier generations of Advance and Scale, are left out, as they already were in an April price increase.

Some charges are being restructured, not just raised. Starting October 1st, storage and IP addresses become separate line items on Gen3 instances, at €0.000146 per GB per hour and €0.0027 per hour. OVHcloud is also dropping the 1-, 6-, and 24-month savings plans, keeping only the 12- and 36-month options, which lock in the price for the contract's duration, a clear sign that the company is betting on cost predictability as a selling point.

results.title: Wegen Arbeitsspeicher: Cloudanbieter OVH macht Server mehr als 80 Prozent teurer - Golem.de
results.author: Oliver Nickel
highlights:
Der französische Cloudanbieter OVH hat drastische Preissteigerungen bei den eigenen Angeboten angekündigt. Offenbar wird das Mieten von Servern bis zu 87 Prozent verteuert. "KI hat einen signifikanten Einfluss auf die Preise von RAM und Speicher", schreibt CEO Octave Klaba auf X(öffnet im neuen Fenster). Aufträge für Bare-Metal-Server ab dem ersten Juli 2026 sollen bereits von Preiserhöhungen bei Optionen für RAM und SSD betroffen sein.

Ab dem ersten September werden die Preiserhöhungen für alle neuen Konfigurationen übernommen. Bestehende Server werden erst verteuert, wenn diese auf neue Hardware umgestellt werden. Diese Phase soll ab dem 1. Oktober beginnen. Dabei erhalten verschiedene Serverkonfigurationen auch unterschiedliche Preissteigerungen.

## Preise von RAM steigen schon jetzt

Ein Gameserver mit Gen2026-Hardware wird um 87 Prozent teurer. Hohe Preissteigerungen werden auch für die Konfigurationen Advance Gen 2024 (26 Prozent), Advance Gen 2026 (49 Prozent), High Grade Gen 2024 (26 Prozent), High Grade Gen 2026 (59 Prozent), Scale Gen 2025 (37 Prozent) und Scale Gen 2026 (40 Prozent) angesetzt. Im Schnitt werden die Preise um 28 Prozent für die ältere 2024-Generation und 51 Prozent für die neueren 2026-Server angehoben.

Bei bereits existierenden Servern werden laut Klaba nur RAM- und SSD-Preise erhöht. Je nach Generation reichen die Preissteigerungen von etwa 20 bis 40 Prozent bei Arbeitsspeicher und 10 bis 15 Prozent bei Massenspeicher. Kunden sollen die aktuellen Preise auch mit einem längeren Abo über 12 oder 24 Monate beziehen können. Es ist wahrscheinlich, dass innerhalb dieser Abozeiten die Preise noch einmal ansteigen.

results.title: EU Sovereign Cloud Providers Pay Spot Prices on Chips
results.author: Andrei Nutas
highlights:
On 10 August 2026, Octave Klaba, the founder and chairman of OVHcloud, one of Europe’s largest independent cloud providers, posted the company’s new prices in a thread on X. Almost everything is going up. The steepest increases fall on the newest dedicated servers, which will cost as much as 87 percent more, and the rises run down the whole catalogue from there, through older machines and into public cloud instances. New orders reprice on 1 September. Renewals follow a month later.

Behind the increases is the cost of memory. Since 1 July, adding RAM to a new OVHcloud order costs 127 percent more, and adding storage 89 percent more. By Klaba’s account, DRAM and NAND prices have risen roughly sixfold year on year through June, he projects ninefold by September and twelvefold by 2027, and the reason is that the manufacture of GPUs and high-bandwidth memory for AI has pulled fabrication capacity away from the ordinary components every server is built around.

...

Which means OVHcloud does not set its own prices. Its cost base moves with the purchasing decisions of the American companies it competes against.

For comparison, Amazon buys DRAM and NAND in the same overheated market. Yet so far its prices have barely moved. It has raised EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, one reserved GPU product, by about 20 percent from July on top of roughly 15 percent in January, and left everything else untouched, including instances running Trainium, the accelerator it designs itself. This was also done without an announcement. The new numbers appeared on the pricing page, and after Business Insider reported them AWS said only that Capacity Blocks prices “are updated periodically based on supply and demand.”
